title: streamline-ephemeral-quarantine-and-capacity-warmup
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem:
The current node quarantine and capacity warmup flow is brittle and a significant source of operational churn. Transient GPU errors and flapping node health probes frequently push nodes into a long-running legacy quarantine path, which triggers conservative warmup policies in the capacity planner. This leads to under-utilized reserved capacity, request routing flaps, and elevated tail latency for affected customers.

Root causes we've identified: compact but opaque lease encodings spread across components, multiple ad-hoc warmup triggers (kube-drain, health-probe-fail, eviction-policy), and race conditions between the autoscaler reclaim loop and the node repair orchestration. The codebase contains legacy adapters (leasepool, old binding controller hooks) that complicate reasoning and make small fixes risky.

Proposal summary:
1) Replace the ad-hoc quarantine predicates with a small phase-based node lifecycle: ACTIVE -> QUARANTINE -> WARMUP -> ACTIVE. Each phase has a single authoritative transition API and well-defined invariants.
2) Introduce a compact epoch+reason lease token (RFC in doc) to replace duplicated lease encodings; the token is intentionally small and easy to inspect in logs and metrics.
3) Move warmup heuristics into the capacity-planner core as tunable policies (grace-period, progressive-weighted-warmup, capacity-reservation-window) and remove the scattered warmup checks in provisioners.
4) Implement a lightweight repair-orchestrator that serializes repairs for a node while exposing a non-blocking cancellation path for the autoscaler.
5) Migration path: feature-flagged rollout with shadow mode (planner sim) for 2 weeks, then opt-in gradual rollout by cluster with canary and traffic mirroring.

Acceptance criteria:
- New lifecycle transitions exercised end-to-end in e2e harness; no regression to existing allocation throughput (<= 5% variance on benchmark).
- Warmup policy config can be updated without restarts and is reflected in the console metrics.
- Lease token present in every allocation event and reconciler log.
- No increase in eviction/requeue rate in production (measured over two weeks).

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Design doc + RFC (done) - https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Phase-based+Quarantine+RFC (link to internal doc).
2) Lease token library + unit tests - branch eng/234567/lease-token (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4567).
3) Capacity planner hookpoints + warmup policy engine - branch eng/234567/warmup-policy (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/capacity/pull/1129).
4) Repair-orchestrator + reconciler cleanup - branch eng/234567/repair-orch (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fleet/pull/789).
5) Canary rollout, dashboards, and alerting - dashboard draft https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/PLT/quarantine-warmup (panel IDs included in PR 789).

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: subtle race where an autoscaler reclaim and repair-orchestra both mark a node for replacement. Mitigation: conservative initial feature flag, serialized repairs, additional metrics and a short-circuit cancel API.
- Risk: mis-tuned warmup causes capacity undershoot. Mitigation: shadow planner mode for 2 weeks and canary by serving pool.

Observability and post-deploy checks:
- New metrics: node_phase_transitions{from,to}, warmup_progress_seconds, lease_token_age_seconds.
- Traces: end-to-end allocation trace includes phase transition events.
- Alert: >3x increase in node_phase_transitions QUARANTINE->WARMUP over baseline for 30m.

Follow-ups (post-migration):
- Replace legacy leasepool adapter in the lease-reader service (ENG-??? follow-up).
- Add a cost analysis job to quantify reduced warmup-induced idle GPU hours.

Notes on trade-offs considered:
- We debated a full event-sourced node lifecycle (more code, stronger guarantees) vs a lightweight phase model. Chose phase model to minimize churn and speed rollout.
- Decided against immediately deleting old adapter code; instead we will deprecate and remove after a clean two-cycle rollout to reduce blast radius.

Estimated effort: ~8 points spread across two sprints. Core work split across infra, capacity, and fleet teams.
